title: Overnight Baseload Drift
dataSources: SolarEdge/Enphase production (`solaredge:power`, `enphase:production`), Powerwall (`powerwall:aggregate`), smart-meter P1/DSMR (`dsmr:telegram`), Emporia Vue (`emporia:circuit`).
app: Solar inverters (SolarEdge/Enphase/Fronius/Growatt), Tesla Powerwall, and smart meters (P1/DSMR, Emporia Vue, Sense) via vendor APIs and MQTT to HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=dsmr:telegram
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| where hour>=1 AND hour<5
| bin _time span=1w
| stats avg(import_kw) as baseload_kw by _time
| streamstats window=4 current=f avg(baseload_kw) as baseline
| where baseline>0 AND baseload_kw>baseline*1.2
| sort - baseload_kw
description: Tracks your sleeping-hours power draw and alerts when the always-on baseline has crept upward beyond the recent norm.
value: Baseload creep is how hidden devices and aging appliances quietly inflate bills; this trend catches the drift before it becomes invisible normal.
implementation: Send smart-meter import power into Splunk; schedule weekly and investigate any sustained overnight load jump.
visualization: Line chart of weekly overnight baseload versus rolling baseline.
grandmaExplanation: It spots when the amount of electricity your home uses while everyone is asleep starts quietly creeping upward.
